name: UC Health

ahrq.src: AHRQ Compendium of U.S. Health Systems, 2023, matched to CMS's hospital list (the site's June 2026 pull)

hc.src: Medicare hospital cost reports (CMS HCRIS, Worksheet S-3), fiscal year 2024 file

subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did University of Cincinnati Medical Center have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital reports more; West Chester Hospital is next at 1,143. About 9.2 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did West Chester Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center has the most, 5,507. About 7.4 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Lindner Center of Hope have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center has the most, 5,507. About 1.6 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians trained at University of Cincinnati Medical Center in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians trained at West Chester Hospital in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do UC Health's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians train in UC Health's hospitals, added together?
questions.why: 2 of its hospitals report residents; University of Cincinnati Medical Center trains the most, 527.

questions.q: What percent of University of Cincinnati Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; West Chester Hospital runs highest, 61 percent. Traditional Medicare was 14 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 29 percent.

questions.q: What percent of West Chester Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital runs higher; University of Cincinnati Medical Center is next at 43 percent. Traditional Medicare was 26 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 35 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Lindner Center of Hope's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 UC Health hospitals; West Chester Hospital runs highest, 61 percent. Traditional Medicare was 8 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 19 percent.

questions.q: What percent of University of Cincinnati Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital runs higher; West Chester Hospital is next at 17 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 6 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 26 percent.

questions.q: What percent of West Chester Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center runs highest, 33 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 4 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 13 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Lindner Center of Hope's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center runs highest, 33 percent. Traditional Medicaid was 1 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 5 percent.

questions.q: Across all of UC Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of UC Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center has the most, 596 beds.

questions.q: How many beds did Lindner Center of Hope report to Medicare for fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center has the most, 596 beds.

questions.why: That is 30 percent of its 596 beds.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds did West Chester Hospital report to Medicare for fiscal 2025?

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did University of Cincinnati Medical Center report for fiscal 2025?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital discharged more; West Chester Hospital is next at 11,046. About 78 a day.

questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center discharged the most, 28,548. About 30 a day.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Lindner Center of Hope report for fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 UC Health hospitals; University of Cincinnati Medical Center discharged the most, 28,548. About 4 a day.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at University of Cincinnati Medical Center in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; Lindner Center of Hope ran longest, 6.6 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at West Chester Hospital in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That is the shortest of 3 UC Health hospitals; Lindner Center of Hope ran longest, 6.6 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Lindner Center of Hope in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital kept patients longer; University of Cincinnati Medical Center is next at 6.4 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2025, what percent of University of Cincinnati Medical Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 UC Health hospitals; West Chester Hospital ran fullest, 84 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2025, what percent of West Chester Hospital's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: No other UC Health hospital ran fuller; University of Cincinnati Medical Center is next at 83 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2025, what percent of Lindner Center of Hope's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That is the emptiest of 3 UC Health hospitals; West Chester Hospital ran fullest, 84 percent.

questions.q: How many hospitals does UC Health run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in Ohio. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: How many beds do UC Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.

questions.q: How many beds does UC Health's biggest hospital report to Medicare?
questions.why: It is University of Cincinnati Medical Center. West Chester Hospital is next, with 154.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds do UC Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: That is 25 percent of their 782 beds. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did UC Health's hospitals report in a year, added together?
questions.why: About 112 a day. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2025.
